# Agent swarm: review → rethink → fix → verify

Learned from a full Stich overhaul (2026-10-13): 4 review agents, 2 holistic reviews, 1 vision
pass, 14 fix lanes, 2 cross-model reviewers. Tests went from 443 to 576, typecheck stayed green,
and the swarm closed a critical public-API hole and a CSS tracking-pixel bypass. Each section
below records what worked and what to do better next time.

## 0. Before spawning anything

- Read the repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) and memory. Every brief must restate
  the rules that matter: command prefixes (e.g. `rtk`), test conventions, and forbidden actions.
- **Check git status.** If the owner has many uncommitted changes, every agent must make surgical
  edits only, re-read files right before editing, never revert others' work, and NEVER
  commit/push/deploy. Check for hooks that deploy on push (Stich's pre-push hook deploys prod).
- Run `orchestrator_capabilities` to get live model IDs. Don't trust a native tool's model list.

## 1. Model routing (the user's stated preference)

| Work | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| UI fixes, refactors, copy | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | low (usually enough) |
| Data layer, security, evals, infra, most fixes | GPT-6.1-Sol | medium |
| Small, iterative fixes (tests, docs, one module) | GPT-6-Luna | medium/high |
| UX & feature-completeness review | GPT-6.1-Sol | high |
| Market/competitive review (web search) | GPT-6-Astra | medium/high |
| "Grand unified" product vision | Claude Fable 5.1 | default |
| Final independent review | a model that wrote little of the code (Opus 5.5 high) | high |

Always pair implementation with a **reviewer on a different model**, allowed to fix confident defects.

## 2. Phase plan

1. **Parallel expert reviews** (read-only): design/UI, tests, AI/evals, architecture. Ask for
   file:line evidence, strengths, weaknesses, and a top-5 list. Run them in the foreground in parallel when
   your next step depends on all of them.
2. **Verify headline claims yourself** before acting. Critical findings get a direct look.
3. **Holistic reviews** (read-only, async): product completeness/UX/practicality, plus
   competitive positioning with cited sources. Feed them the earlier findings and say "don't
   re-report these", which pushes them toward new ground.
4. **Vision pass** (Fable): one organizing principle that reshapes data model, AI stack, UX,
   evals, and go-to-market. Ask for a model-portfolio table and a phased roadmap mapped to file
   paths, then build phase 1 from it. Verify its external claims (endpoint names, model releases).
5. **Fix lanes** in waves. A wave is a set of agents with **disjoint file scopes**. Defer lanes
   that would touch the same files to the next wave (composer/sanitizer waited on the reviewer;
   big component splits went last).
6. **Independent reviewer** after each risky wave, then a **final cross-model review** of everything.
7. **Own the final gate**: full typecheck + full tests with no agent running, plus your own
   probes of security-sensitive code.

## 3. Writing briefs that work

Every implementation brief contains:
- Repo path, "read AGENTS.md first", and the key project rules restated.
- **SCOPE** (exact files/dirs it owns) and **DO NOT TOUCH** (files other live agents own). For
  shared files (e.g. `index.ts`, `package.json`), allow additive one-line edits only.
- Numbered tasks with "verify each first" and the evidence from the review (file:line).
- Behavioural guardrails: "pure refactor: DOM, labels, test IDs, stories identical", "defaults
  must be byte-identical; add a test proving it", "snapshot must match WITHOUT updating".
- **RESOURCE RULE**: iterate with focused `--filter` tests and package typecheck, and run the full
  suite ONCE at the end. Five agents running full suites at once OOM-killed checks (exit 137/144).
- Deliverable: a word cap, files changed, tests added, what was deferred, and **which failures
  are yours vs. other in-flight agents'**.
- Distinct, stable `clientRequestId` per lane and per retry.

Research/review briefs add: read-only, a cap on searches and file reads, and "ALWAYS deliver the final report even if partial".

## 4. Failure modes seen, and the fix for each

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Codex (Sol/Astra) run cancelled before reporting | Retry with a tighter budget, "always deliver", and the partial findings passed in |
| Parent session restart cancels ALL in-flight Codex children (Claude children resume) | Relaunch with a "RESUME: inspect `git diff` of your scope and continue from partial edits" brief, plus the known breakage listed |
| Agent "fixes" a cross-package import with a new dependency cycle | Name the cycle in the brief; prefer dependency injection (we injected the agent transport into `@stich/ai` evals) |
| Agent leaves failures it calls "outside my scope" (date-pinned fixtures vs. real clock) | Re-run that package yourself; fix or send it back |
| Agent's own tests pass but a bypass remains (CSS `image-set("…")`) | Probe security code yourself with an adversarial payload list |
| Agent works around a missing API in a file it doesn't own (fake "Re:" compose) | Note it, and have the owning lane add a proper API and remove the workaround |
| Your own fix is wrong (trusted a caller-controlled `x-forwarded-host`) | That is what the independent reviewer is for. Always run one on security changes |
| Mid-edit typecheck noise from other lanes | Attribute errors by file ownership before blaming anyone; re-check when that lane finishes |
| Running agent breaks a guardrail test | Steer it live with `t3_thread_send` mode `steer` instead of waiting |

Guardrail tests built early pay off. A workspace-boundary test caught three later violations.

## 5. Verification checklist (you, not agents)

- [ ] Full typecheck and full test suite green with **no agents running**; save logs to /tmp.
- [ ] Security probes: header spoofing on privileged routes, private/DNS-rebinding model URLs,
      sanitizer payloads (svg onload, mXSS, `@import` in `@media`, `\75 rl`, `u/**/rl`,
      `image-set("…")`, `cross-fade`, `@font-face src`, `//host`, `</style>` breakout).
- [ ] Boundary/cycle check: no package imports an app; no new allowlist entries.
- [ ] Synthetic eval scores are labelled as such. Never present them as model quality.
- [ ] Marketing claims match shipped code (mobile, drafts, hosting, "local models", "AI acts").
- [ ] Nothing committed or pushed; tell the user what remains unverified (live server, browser).

## 6. Improving the application itself (lessons that generalise)

- **Lock down before you build.** Embedded services behind a public proxy inherit its exposure;
  trust socket peers, never Host/Origin/forwarded headers.
- **Untrusted content stays out of the system prompt.** Wrap it (`<untrusted_…>`), say it's data,
  and state plainly when the model has no tools.
- **Evals before tuning.** Golden set + red-team set + replay cassettes in CI + live mode opt-in,
  scoring calibration (Brier/ECE) and gate precision, not just accuracy.
- **Turn user corrections into the moat.** Store content-free correction records, calibrate
  per user (isotonic, fall back to defaults below ~50 samples), and export them as the eval set.
- **Use a portfolio of models**, each where it's strongest: on-device static/late-interaction
  embeddings for retrieval, typed decision APIs for routing and approvals, tabular models for
  "will I reply", and generative LLMs only for drafting and summaries.
- **Position on what competitors structurally can't copy**, and rewrite copy to claim only what
  ships.

## 7. Report to the user

After each lane: what changed, how you verified it, and what you corrected or rejected. Keep it short.
At the end: final verification numbers, what is unverified, deferred items, and the next phase.
Save new durable lessons to memory and update this skill.

content.thinking:
I'm realizing the fixed bottom-right dock still risks covering text on narrow screens for the in-flow popover, since it's positioned below the passage at the left edge. I need a smarter fallback that docks the popover somewhere it won't overlap the reading content, rather than just copying the flow-dock position.

Actually with the canvas at 768 centered in 1278, margins come to 255px each side, too narrow for the card. Shrinking the card doesn't help enough either, so I consider shifting the whole page left to open up room on the right, similar to how Google Docs shifts the page when comments are present — though that introduces layout jumps whenever margin content appears, which feels risky. I need to think about what's actually realistic to build and review given the effort constraints.

For execution, I'm reading the user's instruction as: have Sonnet handle most tasks at low or medium effort while I (Opus) do the reviewing, which also satisfies the cross-model review guidance. Now I'm breaking the work into lanes with separate file scopes, starting with a small CSS/layout bug fix across living-desk.css and document-spine.tsx.

I'm also checking that the data-flow hiding logic in document-spine.tsx matches value against "flow" or "settling" rather than just checking attribute presence, and confirming the panel component doesn't need the same fix since earlier greps only flagged document-spine.tsx and the CSS file. I need to figure out whether "settling" mode should keep the panel dimmed rather than fully hidden, since that state represents a transitional dimming rather than full suppression.

Separately, flow mode already triggers zenMode through the focus dispatch, which likely hides the LivingDeskPanel on its own, so the CSS hiding rule might be redundant there — I should restrict the CSS fix to flow mode and let settling handle dimming instead. I also want to improve the spine cap's hit area, since its current 12×19px size is too small for easy discovery and interaction.

Next, the board-closing-on-manuscript-focus bug: I need to check whether the editorial board overlays the manuscript or sits as a flex sibling, since the fix should only close the board at narrow viewport widths where it covers the manuscript, not on wide desktop layouts where it pushes content aside.

For lane division, I'm also thinking about shared edits to global.css — since multiple lanes may touch it, I need a strategy for safe concurrent editing, like assigning separate sections or line ranges per lane rather than letting agents collide on the same regions.

Mapping out where each lane's CSS rules actually live in global.css — the in-flow, flow, selection-actions, editorial-overlay, and live-review-status blocks are scattered across different line ranges, plus separate component CSS files for living-desk and sentence-bench. I'll instruct each lane to only touch their specific rule blocks, re-read the exact region right before editing, and never use Write on the shared global.css file.

The bigger architectural issue is two systems fighting over the same UI space — the real fix is making the struggle tracker defer to the conductor, skipping auto-open when conductor mode is "flow" or "settling" while still allowing manual opens via selection. I need to check whether struggle-tracker and flow-conductor have circular import dependencies before wiring this gate in, since flow-conductor already pulls in idb and house-store, and struggle-tracker likely shares some of those imports too.

Actually the real conflict isn't layout but attention — two competing suggestions firing at once. I think the simplest fix is to have the struggle tracker stay quiet while the conductor is in flow or settling mode, only allowing manual opens like selecting text for the sentence bench, and to share a single width breakpoint constant between the two systems.

For the in-flow popover, I want to switch its fallback position from covering the passage text to the same bottom-right dock as the flow card, with a capped width and max-height so it can't eat the screen. The issue is that if both docks are active they'd overlap in the same corner, so either the flow dock should hide itself when an in-flow tool is docked, or the two cards should stack vertically.

I'm thinking a CSS `:has()` selector on a shared parent container is the cleanest way to hide the flow dock whenever an in-flow popover is present, since it's supported in modern Chromium, Safari, and Firefox — effectively the live tool claims the corner while margin cards defer. I also want to double check that docking bottom-right at common viewport widths (like 1280 with a centered 768px page) doesn't end up overlapping the page content itself.

Checking the overlap math more closely, at 1280px the dock only eats into about 29px of the text's bottom-right corner, which is far less intrusive than covering the passage center. But at 1024px with the board panel open, the dock is positioned fixed relative to the viewport, so it ends up sitting on top of the board instead of avoiding it — I think the fix is to position the dock relative to the scroller's actual bounding rect rather than the viewport.

I'm also weighing a Google Docs-style shifted-margin approach versus the dock: that only works when the scroller width leaves enough room for both the page and a margin rail, and running the numbers across viewport sizes with the board open/closed, the margin only reliably fits at wider breakpoints — narrower ones still need the dock.

Shifting the page sideways whenever a tool activates feels too jarring during active editing, so I'll deprioritize it as a follow-up idea and focus on the dock pattern for narrow widths.

For narrow mode, I'll fix the dock to the bottom-right of the manuscript scroller itself rather than the viewport, capping its width and height with internal scrolling, and accept that the cursor could occasionally hide behind it for this pass — a reasonable tradeoff given the simpler implementation. That settles the narrow dock behavior, so now I need to address the Sentence Bench density issue.

For trimming the Sentence Bench and margin card chrome, I'm planning several changes: making the close button meet a proper tap target size, collapsing the "Ask the room" section behind a disclosure toggle, shrinking the repeated paragraph context down to just one sentence on each side (or hiding it behind a "Show paragraph" toggle), and leaving the footer notice as-is since it's already quiet enough. I'm also weighing whether to drop the decorative instrument art from the margin card, since it adds height but is tied to the visual identity.

I'm now thinking the illustration could just shrink to something smaller and sit inline with the title rather than being removed outright. I'm also sketching out which files belong to which lane of work — grouping margin-rail.tsx, sentence-bench.tsx/css, tool-renderer.tsx, and the related in-flow CSS together as one lane, while figuring out whether struggle-tracker and flow-surface belong in that same lane or a separate one given their overlap with margin-rail.

For the next item, I'm thinking about trimming the selection toolbar down to just 3-4 core verbs plus a "More" option, touching selection-actions.tsx, its CSS block, and the twyne-editor.tsx call site while keeping the props interface unchanged.

I'm sketching the primary row as "Rework," "Find sources," "Comment," and an "Ask an editor" persona menu, with secondary actions like Hear, Threads, Scene bench, and Task desk tucked under "More" — possibly renaming them to plainer verbs like "Read aloud" or "Trace threads," though I'd leave the final wording to the implementing lane. I also want to flag that the toolbar's placement logic currently overlaps the paragraph text above it, which needs fixing.

Now I'm thinking through the toolbar sizing in twine-editor.tsx: shrinking it to one row (~36px) above the selection keeps it from covering too much text, similar to how Medium or Google Docs position their selection toolbars. For lane E's work on selection-actions.tsx and its styles, I need to grep the e2e and test suites for hardcoded label strings like "Sentence bench," "Get sources," "Add margin," and "Send to persona," since renaming labels could break tests that reference them directly. I'm also weighing naming choices like "Cast" versus "Room of Editors" for the tools panel, which would touch board-tabs.ts and other editor files.

I'm scoping the naming pass narrowly, considering renaming the "Cast" tab to "Editors" while keeping "The Room of Editors" as the panel heading since it already contains "Editors," and updating related labels like "CAST"/"EDIT CAST →" to something like "EDITORS"/"Manage editors →." I also want to check the sidebar, personas panel header, and margin-rail shelf label ("Your tools") for consistency, plus consider renaming the "Tools" tab (grammar and writing checks) to something like "Checks," while being careful about tests that might assert on these exact labels in board tabs or landing preview components.

Since the shelf rename touches margin-rail.tsx which belongs to Lane C, I should hand that off to Lane C, while the board tabs, personas panel, and sidebar changes go to Lane B along with the route.

On silent failures, LiveReviewStatus hides itself as sr-only when idle, so I want a visible fallback — the status bar at the bottom already shows manuscript stats, and it's a natural place to surface something like "Review paused: no provider" with a settings link instead of hiding it entirely.

The LiveReviewStatus line can cover this: "Reviews and margin notes need a model · Connect" using the same hasConfiguredAiProvider check the struggle-tracker uses. I'm also noticing the empty "Your tools" aside still renders at 176px wide even with nothing saved, and since the rail CSS makes all children pointer-events auto, that empty strip actually captures clicks in the left margin and adds an empty "Your tools" landmark for accessibility tools too.

The fix needs to disable pointer-events on the aside unless it holds saved tools, and swap the landmark role for a plain div when empty, since ticks still render inside it. For smaller polish, I'm noting the 112px masthead that wraps awkwardly at 1024px, the board's bulky 3×2 tab grid that should collapse into a scrollable single row, and the persona panel's four unexplained triggers (Get notes, Propose edits, Run full analysis, room reads on) which need tooltips or helper text to clarify their differences.

I'm also flagging inconsistent close buttons — a 56px box on the Board versus a 7px one on cards — and want to shrink Board's to 32px and enlarge cards' to 24px. The sidebar drawer showing the full dossier card before folios pushes content below the fold, so I need to locate that drawer component to fix the ordering.

Given how many lanes are piling up, I'm now organizing everything into parallel waves with disjoint file scopes — starting with Lane A covering the living desk files and Lane B covering the board and route files, assigning each to appropriate model tiers.

CONTEXT (verified in a browser at 1440/1280/1024 widths):
- Two independent systems fill the same margins. MarginRails (margin-rail.tsx, fed by struggle-tracker.ts) shows ONE live tool card in the right margin (CARD_WIDTH 296) and a "Your tools" shelf in the left margin; when the right margin is < 296+28+8 = 332px it switches to a position:fixed "popover" placed directly under the passage (popTop = anchor rect.bottom + 10) — covering the text the tool is about. FlowSurface (flow-surface.tsx ~272, fed by flow-conductor.ts) puts room cards on the right (ROOM_WIDTH 268) and archive cards on the left; when right room is < 268+28+8 = 304 it switches to a fixed bottom-right dock (.flow-dock / .flow-desk--dock at right:16px of the VIEWPORT). Between 304 and 332px, room cards sit in the rail while the tool pops over the text.
- At 1280×800 the page's right margin is ~255px → the Sentence Bench popover covers the paragraph. At 1024 with the Editorial Board open (a ~29rem flex sibling at the viewport's right edge), the manuscript column is ~558px wide and the popover covers half of it; the viewport-anchored dock (right:16px) lands on top of the Board.

- The in-flow card's close button (.in-flow-card__close "✕") renders ~7×19px.
- "Your tools" (this margin shelf), "Tools" (an Editorial Board tab: grammar & checks) and "Writing tools" (sidebar) are three different things.

1. One geometry: create src/utils/margin-geometry.ts with the shared constants (gutter 28, room card width 268, tool card max 296, archive width 212 as used today) and a pure function that, given measured right/left room, returns rail-vs-dock for the right margin, whether the left column fits, and the tool card width (clamp between the room card width and 296, so the tool card shrinks before it gives up). Use it in both MarginRails and FlowSurface so they switch at the same breakpoint. Add a small bun unit test next to it (src/utils/margin-geometry.test.ts).
2. One narrow fallback that never covers the text uninvited: replace MarginRails' under-the-passage popover with a dock in the same corner as FlowSurface's dock. In the dock, a tool the tracker opened by itself appears COLLAPSED as a small chip (tool name + "Open"); a tool the writer explicitly asked for (selection toolbar button, a saved tool, etc. — trace how open() is reached; add e.g. `requested: true` on ActiveTool if needed) opens EXPANDED. Expanded dock card: max-height ≈ 60vh, scrolls internally, has a collapse control. Apply the same idea to FlowSurface's dock: start collapsed (one-line chip "N from the room · Open"), EXCEPT when the conductor's mode is "stuck" (it deliberately offers the single best thing then). Rail-mode behavior (connector, underline, card placement) stays unchanged.
3. Anchor both docks to the manuscript column, not the viewport: compute the right offset from the scroller's rect (window.innerWidth − scrollerRect.right + 16), the way FlowSurface already computes dockBottom, and pass it as a CSS variable. The two docks must not overlap each other — there's an existing body:has(.in-flow-rail, .in-flow-popover, …) rule near global.css ~7780 that hides the flow dock while an in-flow card is up; keep that coherent with your new class names.
4. Defer to the conductor: in struggle-tracker.ts evaluate() (the automatic path, ~line 648), don't auto-open a tool while the conductor is enabled and its mode is "flow" or "settling". Prefer importing flowSnapshot from "./flow-conductor" (check no import cycle results; flow-conductor does not import struggle-tracker today). Explicit opens are unaffected. Don't change struggle detection itself.
5. Card chrome: close button hit area ≥ 24×24 (keep it visually quiet). Rename the margin shelf "Your tools" → "Saved tools", and related strings: "Keep this tool" → "Save this tool", "In Your tools" → "Saved", struggle-tracker notices "Kept in Your tools." / "From Your tools: …" accordingly. When nothing is saved, don't expose an empty "Saved tools" complementary landmark (the aside still hosts the paragraph ticks — drop its role/label while empty, or similar).
6. grep src/tests/e2e for every class/string you change (in-flow-popover, in-flow-rail, flow-dock, flow-desk--dock, "Your tools", "Keep this tool", …); update affected unit tests and e2e selectors (e2e can't be run here — edit carefully) and run the affected unit tests once.

---
name: twyne-browser-verification
description: How to check twyne editor UI in a real browser here — headless Playwright env fix, free port, IndexedDB folio seeding, known flaky test pair
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Recipe that worked on 2026-10-17 for verifying editor UI changes without the Convex backend:

- **Port:** 5173 may belong to another project (interleave-app). Start twyne with `TWYNE_DEV_PORT=5174 bun run dev.frontend`.
- **Headless Playwright:** importing `node_modules/playwright/index.mjs` from a scratch script works, but Chromium fails to launch (GLIBC error from a nix alsa-lib) unless run as `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH node script.mjs`.
- **Skip onboarding:** a fresh profile redirects /editor/ to /dossier/create/. Instead, seed like `e2e/instruments.e2e.ts` `seed()`: route `/api/auth/` to `null`, visit a routed blank page, `import("/src/utils/idb.ts")` in page context, then call saveFoliosToIdb / saveFolioContentToIdb / saveActiveFolioIdToIdb (+ `signin-toast-dismissed` meta, `twyne:editor:view:v1` with zenMode false).
- **T3 preview tool:** its viewport can be zoomed or scaled (innerWidth ≠ the requested size), and evaluate/snapshot time out on heavy pages. Prefer the headless script for measurements.
- **Known flaky pair (pre-existing at HEAD bfa07af1):** `struggle-tracker.test.ts` and `quick-review.test.ts` fail together in one bun run (shared System One budget state). Each passes alone. Don't blame new changes for it.

---
name: agent-swarm-app-improvement
description: >
  Run a multi-model agent swarm (T3 delegate_task / Agent tool) to review, rethink, and fix an
  application end to end: parallel expert reviews, holistic product/competitive analysis, a
  "grand unified" vision pass, scoped parallel fix lanes, an independent cross-model reviewer,
  and verification gates. Use when the user asks to review a repo from several angles, "spin up
  subagents", fix many issues at once, use specific models (Sonnet/Sol/Luna/Astra/Fable/Opus),
  improve product positioning, or "fully utilize the agent swarm". Not for single small fixes.
---

# Agent swarm: review → rethink → fix → verify

Learned from a full Stich overhaul (2026-10-13): 4 review agents, 2 holistic reviews, 1 vision
pass, 14 fix lanes, 2 cross-model reviewers. Tests went from 443 to 576, typecheck stayed green,
and the swarm closed a critical public-API hole and a CSS tracking-pixel bypass. Each section
below records what worked and what to do better next time.

## 0. Before spawning anything

- Read the repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md) and memory. Every brief must restate
  the rules that matter: command prefixes (e.g. `rtk`), test conventions, and forbidden actions.
- **Check git status.** If the owner has many uncommitted changes, every agent must make surgical
  edits only, re-read files right before editing, never revert others' work, and NEVER
  commit/push/deploy. Check for hooks that deploy on push (Stich's pre-push hook deploys prod).
- Run `orchestrator_capabilities` to get live model IDs. Don't trust a native tool's model list.

## 1. Model routing (the user's stated preference)

| Work | Model | Effort |
|---|---|---|
| UI fixes, refactors, copy | Claude Sonnet 5.5 | low (usually enough) |
| Data layer, security, evals, infra, most fixes | GPT-6.1-Sol | medium |
| Small, iterative fixes (tests, docs, one module) | GPT-6-Luna | medium/high |
| UX & feature-completeness review | GPT-6.1-Sol | high |
| Market/competitive review (web search) | GPT-6-Astra | medium/high |
| "Grand unified" product vision | Claude Fable 5.1 | default |
| Final independent review | a model that wrote little of the code (Opus 5.5 high) | high |

Always pair implementation with a **reviewer on a different model**, allowed to fix confident defects.

## 2. Phase plan

1. **Parallel expert reviews** (read-only): design/UI, tests, AI/evals, architecture. Ask for
   file:line evidence, strengths, weaknesses, and a top-5 list. Run them in the foreground in parallel when
   your next step depends on all of them.
2. **Verify headline claims yourself** before acting. Critical findings get a direct look.
3. **Holistic reviews** (read-only, async): product completeness/UX/practicality, plus
   competitive positioning with cited sources. Feed them the earlier findings and say "don't
   re-report these", which pushes them toward new ground.
4. **Vision pass** (Fable): one organizing principle that reshapes data model, AI stack, UX,
   evals, and go-to-market. Ask for a model-portfolio table and a phased roadmap mapped to file
   paths, then build phase 1 from it. Verify its external claims (endpoint names, model releases).
5. **Fix lanes** in waves. A wave is a set of agents with **disjoint file scopes**. Defer lanes
   that would touch the same files to the next wave (composer/sanitizer waited on the reviewer;
   big component splits went last).
6. **Independent reviewer** after each risky wave, then a **final cross-model review** of everything.
7. **Own the final gate**: full typecheck + full tests with no agent running, plus your own
   probes of security-sensitive code.

## 3. Writing briefs that work

Every implementation brief contains:
- Repo path, "read AGENTS.md first", and the key project rules restated.
- **SCOPE** (exact files/dirs it owns) and **DO NOT TOUCH** (files other live agents own). For
  shared files (e.g. `index.ts`, `package.json`), allow additive one-line edits only.
- Numbered tasks with "verify each first" and the evidence from the review (file:line).
- Behavioural guardrails: "pure refactor: DOM, labels, test IDs, stories identical", "defaults
  must be byte-identical; add a test proving it", "snapshot must match WITHOUT updating".
- **RESOURCE RULE**: iterate with focused `--filter` tests and package typecheck, and run the full
  suite ONCE at the end. Five agents running full suites at once OOM-killed checks (exit 137/144).
- Deliverable: a word cap, files changed, tests added, what was deferred, and **which failures
  are yours vs. other in-flight agents'**.
- Distinct, stable `clientRequestId` per lane and per retry.

Research/review briefs add: read-only, a cap on searches and file reads, and "ALWAYS deliver the final report even if partial".

## 4. Failure modes seen, and the fix for each

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Codex (Sol/Astra) run cancelled before reporting | Retry with a tighter budget, "always deliver", and the partial findings passed in |
| Parent session restart cancels ALL in-flight Codex children (Claude children resume) | Relaunch with a "RESUME: inspect `git diff` of your scope and continue from partial edits" brief, plus the known breakage listed |
| Agent "fixes" a cross-package import with a new dependency cycle | Name the cycle in the brief; prefer dependency injection (we injected the agent transport into `@stich/ai` evals) |
| Agent leaves failures it calls "outside my scope" (date-pinned fixtures vs. real clock) | Re-run that package yourself; fix or send it back |
| Agent's own tests pass but a bypass remains (CSS `image-set("…")`) | Probe security code yourself with an adversarial payload list |
| Agent works around a missing API in a file it doesn't own (fake "Re:" compose) | Note it, and have the owning lane add a proper API and remove the workaround |
| Your own fix is wrong (trusted a caller-controlled `x-forwarded-host`) | That is what the independent reviewer is for. Always run one on security changes |
| Mid-edit typecheck noise from other lanes | Attribute errors by file ownership before blaming anyone; re-check when that lane finishes |
| Running agent breaks a guardrail test | Steer it live with `t3_thread_send` mode `steer` instead of waiting |

Guardrail tests built early pay off. A workspace-boundary test caught three later violations.

## 5. Verification checklist (you, not agents)

- [ ] Full typecheck and full test suite green with **no agents running**; save logs to /tmp.
- [ ] Security probes: header spoofing on privileged routes, private/DNS-rebinding model URLs,
      sanitizer payloads (svg onload, mXSS, `@import` in `@media`, `\75 rl`, `u/**/rl`,
      `image-set("…")`, `cross-fade`, `@font-face src`, `//host`, `</style>` breakout).
- [ ] Boundary/cycle check: no package imports an app; no new allowlist entries.
- [ ] Synthetic eval scores are labelled as such. Never present them as model quality.
- [ ] Marketing claims match shipped code (mobile, drafts, hosting, "local models", "AI acts").
- [ ] Nothing committed or pushed; tell the user what remains unverified (live server, browser).

## 6. Improving the application itself (lessons that generalise)

- **Lock down before you build.** Embedded services behind a public proxy inherit its exposure;
  trust socket peers, never Host/Origin/forwarded headers.
- **Untrusted content stays out of the system prompt.** Wrap it (`<untrusted_…>`), say it's data,
  and state plainly when the model has no tools.
- **Evals before tuning.** Golden set + red-team set + replay cassettes in CI + live mode opt-in,
  scoring calibration (Brier/ECE) and gate precision, not just accuracy.
- **Turn user corrections into the moat.** Store content-free correction records, calibrate
  per user (isotonic, fall back to defaults below ~50 samples), and export them as the eval set.
- **Use a portfolio of models**, each where it's strongest: on-device static/late-interaction
  embeddings for retrieval, typed decision APIs for routing and approvals, tabular models for
  "will I reply", and generative LLMs only for drafting and summaries.
- **Position on what competitors structurally can't copy**, and rewrite copy to claim only what
  ships.

## 7. Report to the user

After each lane: what changed, how you verified it, and what you corrected or rejected. Keep it short.
At the end: final verification numbers, what is unverified, deferred items, and the next phase.
Save new durable lessons to memory and update this skill.

Now I'm cataloguing the remaining bugs by lane: a sideways scroll at 390px from the nowrap masthead (fixed via container query, plus the masthead height correction from 112 to 78), a strict-mode type error in the bench lane, a persona menu that could stay open across selections, and a dead CSS rule left behind in sentence-bench.css.

For verification, I'm running through what passed — 74 unit tests across 8 files including 6 new ones for margin geometry, with one pre-existing flaky pairing that only fails when run together, plus clean typecheck and lint, and manual checks at five viewport widths. I'm also noting what I deliberately didn't run: the full test suite, full tsc, and the Playwright e2e suite.

Now I'm listing the deferred items that weren't addressed this pass — a persistent wordmark overflow at 800px, leftover naming inconsistency between "Writing tools" and "Tools," a stale e2e expectation, a settings link without anchor targeting, and missing arrow-key navigation in the selection toolbar menus. content.text:
Seven Sonnet 5.5 agents made the fixes in parallel: low effort for the three small ones, medium for the four larger ones. I reviewed every diff myself, fixed the problems I found, and measured the result in a headless browser. Nothing is committed: 23 files are modified and 2 are new.

**Before and after (measured):**

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| The Piece (Living Desk) while writing | Couldn't open | Opens; spine button has a 24px target and a hover label |
| Editorial Board while editing | Closed on every click into the text | Stays open; closes only below 720px, where it covers the text. Escape closes it |
| Board tabs | 3×2 grid, ~100px | One row, 40px, all six labels readable. "The Room of Editors" heading → "The Cast" |
| Masthead at 1024 with Board open | 142px, button wrapped | 78px; kicker and dateline step aside when there's no room |
| Selection toolbar | Two rows, 98px, 8 actions | One row, 37px: Rework · Find sources · Comment · Ask an editor ▾ · More ▾ |
| Sentence Bench | ~1,240px tall, 7×19 close button | 716px, 24×24 close button; "Ask an editor" and the full paragraph are collapsed |
| Tool card at 1280px | Covered the passage | Docks in the column's corner, clear of the passage |
| Review problems | Announced to screen readers only | Dismissible one-line notice after 2s, with a "Sign in" or "Set up a model" link |

Behind those:
- Both margin systems now switch layouts at the same width, using a new shared `src/utils/margin-geometry.ts`.
- The struggle tracker no longer opens tools on its own while the writer is in focus.
- Tools that open on their own start as a small chip in the dock; ones the writer asked for open expanded.
- Folios now sit above the dossier card in the sidebar.
- "Your tools" is now "Saved tools", and "Add margin" is now "Comment".

**Problems in the agents' work that I fixed:**
- **Review notice:** it would have cleared on every keystroke and treated "paused" (the writer's own choice) as a problem. It also didn't remember being dismissed, and repeated every routine status to screen readers.
- **Masthead:** the agent's no-wrap change pushed the Board 142px off-screen at 390px wide. A container query replaced it.
- **Sentence Bench:** a type error.
- **Selection toolbar:** the persona menu could stay open from one selection to the next.
- **Leftovers:** a dead CSS rule and a stale comment.

**Checks:**
- **Unit tests:** the targeted tests for the changed areas pass (74 across 8 files), including the new margin-geometry tests. `struggle-tracker.test.ts` and `quick-review.test.ts` fail when run together, but they fail the same way on unmodified HEAD and each passes alone.
- **Typecheck and lint:** clean for the changed files and their imports.
- **Browser:** layouts measured at 390, 700, 800, 1024, 1280 and 1440px.

**Not verified:**
- The full test suite and full `tsc` weren't run, per your earlier preference.
- I updated selectors in three e2e files (`instruments`, `instrument-room`, `instrument-dock`) but didn't run them.
- Anything that needs the Convex backend is untested: AI-filled margin cards, the room's dock chip, and persona threads.

**Still open:**
- At 800px with the Board open, the TWYNE wordmark still overflows its column. That was already true before.
- "Writing tools" in the sidebar and the "Tools" Board tab are still two names for different things.
- "Set up a model" opens the top of Settings, because there's no anchor for the model section.
- The toolbar menus have no arrow-key navigation.
- `e2e/drag-selection.e2e.ts:145` was already out of date before these changes.

I also saved a memory note on checking Twyne in a browser here (use port 5174, a launch fix for headless Chromium, and how to seed a folio).

content.thinking:
I need to tackle the open issues: the wordmark overflow at 800px with the Board open, the naming mismatch between "Writing tools" and "Tools," the lack of an anchor for the model section in Settings, missing arrow-key navigation in toolbar menus, and a failing drag-selection test.

There's also the question of whether to verify my fixes — e2e tests haven't been run, and the full TypeScript check hasn't either. I'm weighing whether running just the drag-selection test is worth it given the environment's quirks with Playwright and dev server startup, and whether I should delegate this work to subagents the way I did for the earlier polish task, since that instruction may or may not still apply here.

Since these five fixes are small and I already have full context, doing them inline seems cheaper than spawning cold agents that would need to re-derive everything. The user's earlier Sonnet-routing preference was tied to that specific polish request rather than a standing instruction, so I don't think it necessarily carries over to this unrelated "fix the open issues" task.

I'll go with inline fixes since they're small and tightly scoped, rather than delegating to Sonnet.

Looking at the first issue: the TWYNE wordmark overflows at 800px when the board panel is open, since the title block only gets 16px of space while the wordmark itself needs 154px. I'm weighing options like shrinking or hiding less-critical header controls to free up room.

Since the font-size is set inline, I can't override it with container-query utility classes directly — I'd need to move it into a class first so container-query variants can take effect. I'm also considering wrapping the header into two rows or collapsing the wordmark into a compact monogram at narrow widths, but I want to figure out what the correct behavior should actually be when the main column shrinks to 334px with the board open.

Doing the math, even collapsing the File button to icon-only and shrinking the wordmark to 1.25rem still doesn't leave enough room for the full TWYNE wordmark — there's just not enough horizontal space at that width no matter how I trim the controls.

Another option is wrapping the header when the column narrows, putting the title on its own row above the controls, but that adds vertical height. Or I could just hide the wordmark entirely below a certain width since the sidebar/board is already providing context, though that sacrifices the brand link that doubles as a home button — worth weighing whether that tradeoff is acceptable.

Maybe a monogram "T" could stand in for the full wordmark at narrow widths, but a second element adds its own width and doesn't shrink enough to actually solve the overflow. Really the root cause is the Board eating 464px of an 800px viewport, so perhaps the better fix is at the layout level — adjusting how much space the Board claims in that mid-range viewport width instead of squeezing the header.

So the real problem is between roughly 721-900px with the board open, the main column gets too narrow and the masthead overflows. I'm thinking about using a container query on the header row so it wraps to two lines when space is tight, forcing the title block to take full width and reorder below the other elements.

A simpler fix might be hiding the wordmark, kicker, and dateline when the title block's container gets too narrow, leaving just the hamburger and controls visible with empty space between them—clean, no overflow, though the branding temporarily disappears.

But checking the numbers at the narrowest Board side-by-side breakpoint around 721px, I find even the controls themselves don't fit within the main column at that width, so the overflow problem exists even before the title block becomes an issue.

Since the main column can't shrink below zero, the controls actually slide underneath the Board overlay at these widths, which hides the Board toggle control — users could still close the Board via its own close button or Escape, but losing the toggle isn't ideal. The masthead really needs a way to compress the controls further at narrow main-column widths, similar to how Refine already collapses to icon-only below 1280px.

I'm thinking container queries could solve this: naming the header row as a container and using a container-based breakpoint to hide the "File" label inside FolioMenu when the row itself gets narrow, rather than relying on viewport width. The tradeoff is this couples FolioMenu to the masthead's container name, which feels like it creates unwanted coupling between components.

Really, the core question is scope: the stated bug is just that the TWYNE wordmark overflows at 800px with the Board open, but the real problem is the whole masthead not fitting in a narrow main column. I want a fix that handles both — hiding wordmark/kicker/dateline as needed and collapsing File to icon-only — so I'm roughly tallying the minimum masthead width with an icon-only File control to see if it actually fits.

Trimming gaps and padding at narrow widths gets things to fit, but that raises a bigger product question: should the Board even sit side-by-side with the manuscript at 721–900px? It might be cleaner to push the overlay breakpoint higher so the Board covers the manuscript whenever the main column would drop below roughly 480px, rather than only at ≤720px.

Thinking through the actual UX, at 800px with the Board open the manuscript column is 334px — workable but tight — so the masthead needs to shrink gracefully instead of overflowing. I'm setting up a container-query-based compact masthead: making the header's inner row a named container, then at a ~576px container breakpoint hiding the "File" label text and tightening gaps, with the title's kicker hidden below an even smaller width.

I'm also planning to shrink the wordmark progressively via container queries — scaling its font size down at smaller container widths and hiding it entirely below a minimum threshold, which means pulling the font-size out of its inline style and moving it into a Tailwind class so the container variants can override it.

Since the title block uses inline-size containment and its own width comes from the flex layout rather than its children, the container query setup is already correct. Now I'm checking whether the controls overflow in the 721–790px range given the hamburger and icon button widths at that breakpoint.

Working through the actual pixel math: controls at 1024px break down to roughly 216px total, with refine at 48px and File's icon-only form around 56px once I subtract the text and gap. That puts controls closer to 188px wide, and when I add up padding, hamburger, gaps, and title space at a 255px row, the total comes to 290px — about 35px over budget even with the title collapsed.

Trying to shave those 35px with smaller padding and gaps gets me close but still a few pixels short at the narrowest widths, which makes me think pixel-shaving isn't the right fix. I'm considering instead whether the account button could be hidden at narrow widths, or whether the board itself should render narrower between 721-900px, but that feels like a separate layout decision. What I actually want is a more robust solution — letting the masthead row wrap naturally when it can't fit, possibly using a container query to trigger that behavior below a certain width.

Actually the better fix might be to raise the side-by-side breakpoint itself — instead of squeezing the main column down to fit both panels at 720px, keep the Board as an overlay until the viewport is wide enough (~980px) to comfortably fit both. That way the masthead and manuscript never get squeezed below their natural minimums, and the overlay-with-shadow behavior already used at narrow widths just extends further up.

I should also update the media query that triggers closing the board when focusing the manuscript, raising its threshold to 960px for consistency — overlaying the board should close it on manuscript focus. I'm weighing whether the 721–960px range is better served by overlay vs push: on tablets like iPad portrait, a 464px board squeezing a 300–370px manuscript column feels cramped, so overlay is likely the more usable pattern there, even though it trades off simultaneous editing while reading the board.

Then I consider a middle ground: keeping side-by-side but scaling the board's width down proportionally within that range using a clamp formula, so the board shrinks to around 320px at narrower widths while still leaving a workable manuscript column, and widening gradually up to its full size near 960px.

But then the 320px board is itself a problem: at that width the tab labels won't fit without shrinking to the small typewriter font used below 720px, which feels increasingly fiddly to coordinate. I'm starting to think I need to step back and reconsider what the real fix is for this interaction issue.

Refocusing on the actual target: the first listed issue is that the wordmark overflows its column at 800px when the board is open, so the minimal fix is to make the masthead degrade gracefully at narrow widths without any element overflowing. I'm now working through the keyboard navigation for the selection toolbar, replacing the Escape-only listener with a unified keyboard handler and adding a root signal to track the container element.

Writing focus navigation logic...

I need to handle focusing the first menu item after it opens via keyboard. Since the closure variable from the trigger's keydown handler isn't visible to a separate task tracking the menu state, I'm considering polling with requestAnimationFrame right after setting the menu open, waiting for the render to complete before focusing the item.

For the mouse-opened case, when the menu is open but focus is still in the editor, pressing ArrowDown/ArrowUp should move focus to the first/last item while preventing default and stopping propagation to preserve the caret, and I should record the editor as the element to return focus to later when Escape is pressed.

For Escape, I'm working out the different cases: if focus is in the menu, close it and return focus to the trigger or editor; if focus is in the editor while the menu's open, close the menu and consume the event so it doesn't bubble to the global dismiss handler; and if there's no menu but focus is on a toolbar row button, let the event propagate to the global handler but first move focus back to the editor so the selection state is preserved when the toolbar disappears.

I'm leaning toward treating Escape like stepping back one level at a time — menu to toolbar to text — so the first press from a toolbar button returns focus to the editor while keeping the toolbar visible (stopping propagation), and a second Escape from within the editor then triggers the editor's own Escape behavior, which blurs and lets the global handler dismiss the toolbar.

For Tab within the menu, I'm following the APG pattern: closing the menu and moving focus to the next tab-sequence element when the focused item isn't in a menubar. I'm working out whether to close the menu and focus the trigger synchronously without preventDefault, since that affects where the browser's default Tab action moves focus from.

Now I'm figuring out arrow key navigation along a row of trigger buttons, closing any open menu when the user moves between row items, and deciding what ArrowDown should do on a closed trigger.

For Enter/Space on a trigger, I'll handle the keydown directly rather than relying on the native click: preventDefault, toggle the menu state myself, and if it opens, focus the first item via a rAF loop, since relying on the native click event makes it harder to know the action came from the keyboard.

In the onClick$ handler, I'll check if event.detail === 0 to detect keyboard activation versus mouse clicks, then focus the first menu item accordingly. I need to make sure focusMenuItem is wrapped as a QRL with $() so it's serializable and accessible within the Qwik component's lexical scope.

For the broader keyboard task — handling Alt+F10, arrow keys, Escape, Tab, and menu triggers — I want to avoid duplicating the focus-retry logic between the visible task and the QRL handler, so I'm considering having the task call the same QRL function instead of reimplementing it locally.

I'll add `data-menu` attributes to triggers to identify which menu they open, and put `aria-keyshortcuts="Alt+F10"` on the toolbar container itself since that's the element the shortcut focuses, which matches the spec's intended usage.

Now I'm checking whether there's a separate shortcut dialog or keybindings list where "Alt+F10 — Move to the selection toolbar" should be documented, rather than just handling it locally in SelectionActions.

I notice the details element appears closed in the snapshot, so its contents aren't expanded in the accessibility tree. That could explain why the locator kept resolving to a disabled button instead of the expected content — collapsed details aren't rendered as visible to role-based queries by default.

My theory is that the Qwik bench component gets re-mounted when the tool transitions from "filling" to "settled," which would reset the native DOM open state of the details element even if the app tries to preserve session state across instance replacement.

This explains the test log: the summary gets clicked and opens the details while the button is still disabled during filling, but then the re-render closes it right as Playwright is polling — so it resolves to the disabled button repeatedly before ultimately timing out with "element(s) not found." My manual check worked because I waited long enough for filling to finish before clicking, avoiding that race entirely.

This is a real bug: the open/disabled disclosure state lives only in local component state (DOM attributes or signals), so it gets wiped whenever the bench instance is replaced after filling completes — snapping a writer's open "Ask an editor" panel shut mid-interaction. The fix is to persist that open state inside the bench session object (keyed by toolId, which survives instance replacement) and make the details element controlled via that persisted value with a toggle handler syncing it back.

I'm investigating why the "More" click registers as highlighted but doesn't open the menu—suspecting that my useTask$ tracking selection text might be resetting store.menu, or that refreshSelectionAction creates a new object that interferes with the click handler even when the text itself hasn't changed.

So the task re-runs any time the parent produces a fresh selectionAction object, even with identical text, and that happens whenever a transaction triggers refreshActive after the click — like pagination remeasures, decoration updates, or other editor transactions. That timing dependency explains the flakiness: in one run the test passed because no transaction fired after the click, but in another it failed because a subsequent transaction caused props.selection to change, re-running my useTask$ and clearing store.menu.

I realize this bug came from code I added myself — the original lane didn't have this task, so my logic for closing the menu when the selection changes is the source of the flakiness. I should guard against spurious reruns by comparing the actual text (or from/to range) against a stored value, only resetting store.menu when the selection truly changed rather than just getting a new object reference.

That explains why the earlier test passed—no background transactions fired during it. The persona menu has the same underlying issue, so the fix should cover both; I'll also re-run the dock suite afterward to confirm nothing regresses. Time to implement the fix.

name: twyne-browser-verification
description: "How to check twyne editor UI in a real browser here — headless Playwright env fix, free port, IndexedDB folio seeding, known flaky test pair"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 2a13dcae-f7b6-4086-b45c-4b7202355290
  modified: 2026-10-17T20:07:11.511Z
---

Recipe that worked on 2026-10-17 for verifying editor UI changes without the Convex backend:

- **Port:** 5173 may belong to another project (interleave-app). Start twyne with `TWYNE_DEV_PORT=5174 bun run dev.frontend`.
- **Headless Playwright:** importing `node_modules/playwright/index.mjs` from a scratch script works, but Chromium fails to launch (GLIBC error from a nix alsa-lib) unless run as `env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH node script.mjs`.
- **Skip onboarding:** a fresh profile redirects /editor/ to /dossier/create/. Instead, seed like `e2e/instruments.e2e.ts` `seed()`: route `/api/auth/` to `null`, visit a routed blank page, `import("/src/utils/idb.ts")` in page context, then call saveFoliosToIdb / saveFolioContentToIdb / saveActiveFolioIdToIdb (+ `signin-toast-dismissed` meta, `twyne:editor:view:v1` with zenMode false).
- **T3 preview tool:** its viewport can be zoomed or scaled (innerWidth ≠ the requested size), and evaluate/snapshot time out on heavy pages. Prefer the headless script for measurements.
- **Known flaky pair (pre-existing at HEAD bfa07af1):** `struggle-tracker.test.ts` and `quick-review.test.ts` fail together in one bun run (shared System One budget state). Each passes alone. Don't blame new changes for it.

Related: [[skip-long-verification]]

content.text:
All five open items are fixed, and I checked each one in a real browser. Running the e2e tests turned up two real bugs from the previous round, which I also fixed. Nothing is committed.

**The five items:**
- **Masthead overflow:** when the Board narrows the column, the TWYNE wordmark now shrinks and then hides, and the header buttons wrap rather than spilling under the Board. Measured at 760–1440px, nothing overflows and the page never scrolls sideways.
  - My first attempt did nothing because the wordmark's existing `.press` rule overrode the Tailwind classes. The sizing is now its own small rule in `global.css`.
- **"Writing tools" vs "Tools":** the sidebar entry is now "Tools", matching the Board tab it opens. The panel's section links are labelled "Tools sections" for screen readers.
- **"Set up a model" link:** it now goes to `/settings/#judgement-model` and scrolls to that section. Settings renders after loading its data, which is later than the router's normal anchor scroll, so the page now scrolls once it has loaded.
- **Keyboard use of the selection toolbar:**
  - Alt+F10 moves focus from the text into the toolbar, and it is listed in the shortcut reference.
  - Left/Right, Home and End move between buttons. Down, Enter or Space opens a menu with focus on its first item. Up/Down move through items and wrap at the ends.
  - Escape closes an open menu, then returns you to the text with the selection kept.
  - On your COSMIC desktop, Alt+F10 is also bound to "maximise window", so the desktop may intercept it before the browser sees it. If so, tell me a shortcut you'd prefer.
- **Stale e2e test:** the pause-review test now uses the Automatic review switch on the Board's Tools tab, and it passes.

**Bugs the e2e runs found:**
- **"Ask the room" was permanently greyed out.** The previous round put the room inside a collapsed section, which stopped it from ever loading the list of editors. It now loads when the section is opened, and the section stays open after the bench redraws.
- **The More and Ask-an-editor menus could close the instant they opened.** Any background editor update reset them, so clicks only sometimes worked. I reproduced it against the old code before fixing it.

**Test results:**
- **e2e:** all six `instrument-room` tests pass. Of 12 in `instruments` and `instrument-dock`, 9 pass. The other 3 fail only because the repo has no committed reference screenshots for this machine; every check before the screenshot step passed. I deleted the screenshots those runs generated.
- **Unit tests:** 100 pass, including a new test for the Alt+F10 binding.
- **Typecheck, lint and Prettier:** clean for every changed file. I ran Prettier on 7 files the agents had left unformatted; all were formatted at HEAD, so only lines changed in this work moved.

**Still not covered:**
- On unmodified HEAD, every test in `e2e/pagination.e2e.ts` and `e2e/drag-selection.e2e.ts` times out waiting for the pagination probe (`__twynePagination`). I confirmed this on a clean copy but didn't diagnose it. I ran the rewritten pause-review test in a temporary copy without that wait.
- Anything that needs the Convex backend is still untested.

My dev servers and the temporary worktree are shut down and removed; the other project on port 5173 was left alone. The memory note now also covers how to run e2e here and the pagination timeout.

import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";

const port = process.env.TWYNE_DEV_PORT || "5173";
const baseURL = `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`;

export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  testMatch: "**/*.e2e.ts",
  timeout: 180_000,
  expect: { timeout: 15_000 },
  fullyParallel: false,
  retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0,
  reporter: process.env.CI ? "github" : "list",
  use: {
    baseURL,
    trace: "retain-on-failure",
    screenshot: "only-on-failure",
    video: "retain-on-failure",
  },
  projects: [
    {
      name: "chromium",
      use: {
        viewport: { width: 1280, height: 900 },
      },
    },
  ],
  webServer: {
    command: "bun run dev.frontend",
    env: { TWYNE_DEV_PORT: port },
    url: baseURL,
    reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
    timeout: 120_000,

});

import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";

const remote = process.env.TWYNE_VISUAL_BASE_URL;
const port = process.env.TWYNE_DEV_PORT || "5187";
const run = new Date().toISOString().replace(/[:.]/g, "-");
const output =
  (process.env.TWYNE_VISUAL_OUTPUT ||= `artifacts/qa-recordings/living-desk/${run}`);

/** Successful runs retain their footage, stills and trace for review and reuse. */
export default defineConfig({
  testDir: "./e2e",
  testMatch: remote
    ? ["manual-living-desk.e2e.ts", "manual-instruments.e2e.ts"]
    : [
        "living-desk.e2e.ts",
        "instruments.e2e.ts",
        "instrument-dock.e2e.ts",
        "instrument-room.e2e.ts",
      ],
  timeout: 90_000,
  expect: { timeout: 15_000, toHaveScreenshot: { maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.005 } },
  workers: 1,
  retries: 0,
  outputDir: `${output}/results`,
  snapshotPathTemplate: "{testDir}/visual-baselines/{testFilePath}/{arg}{ext}",
  reporter: [
    ["list"],
    ["html", { outputFolder: `${output}/report`, open: "never" }],
  ],
  use: {
    baseURL: remote || `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
    actionTimeout: 15_000,
    viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 },
    contextOptions: { reducedMotion: "reduce" },
    locale: "en-CA",
    colorScheme: "light",
    trace: "on",
    screenshot: "on",
    video: { mode: "on", size: { width: 1440, height: 900 } },
  },
  projects: [{ name: "chromium", use: { browserName: "chromium" } }],
  ...(remote
    ? {}
    : {
        webServer: {
          command: "bun run dev.frontend",
          env: { TWYNE_DEV_PORT: port, TWYNE_VISUAL_RUN: "1" },
          url: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
          reuseExistingServer: false,
          timeout: 120_000,
        },
      }),
});
---
import { defineConfig } from "@playwright/test";
import visual from "./playwright.visual.config";

const remote = process.env.TWYNE_VISUAL_BASE_URL;
const port = process.env.TWYNE_MANUAL_PORT || "3139";

/** Exercise Qwik's built resumable page and the actual media range handler. */
export default defineConfig({
  ...visual,
  testMatch: ["manual-living-desk.e2e.ts", "manual-instruments.e2e.ts"],
  use: { ...visual.use, baseURL: remote || `http://127.0.0.1:${port}` },
  webServer: remote
    ? undefined
    : {
        command:
          process.env.TWYNE_MANUAL_PREBUILT === "1"
            ? "bun server.js"
            : "bun run build && bun server.js",
        env: { PORT: port },
        url: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/docs/`,
        reuseExistingServer: false,
        timeout: 240_000,
      },
});

I ran 25 of the 30 e2e files, about 100 tests. None of the failures come from these changes: every test that fails with them also fails on unmodified HEAD.

| Suites | Result |
|---|---|
| instruments, instrument-dock, instrument-room, living-desk | All 27 pass, compared against the committed reference screenshots |
| flow-surface; Typst editor, export and storage; sign-in; PostHog isolation; live voice; house UI | All pass (5 skipped by their own environment checks) |
| byok-settings, draft-navigation, editor-typing | Pass. Some failed on a first cold run on both trees, then passed on rerun |
| editor-declutter, __responsive, select-all, read-aloud | 13 fail, and the same 13 fail on HEAD |
| pagination, formatting, drag-selection | 18 fail, and the same 18 fail on HEAD |
| import, dossier-persistence | 3 fail on the same lines on HEAD |

**What I changed:** I replaced the two Sentence Bench reference screenshots in `e2e/visual-baselines/instruments.e2e.ts/` with the compacted card. The old ones were already out of date: they show the subtitle "Opened from the rubric," which no longer exists in the code. With the new images, the instruments suite passes 6/6.

**The 34 failures that predate this work have four causes:**
- **Pagination:** the pagination extension was taken out of the editor in commit `0cb77885`, so the page-measurement value these tests wait for (`__twynePagination`) never appears. That breaks all of pagination and formatting and most of drag-selection.
  - Without that wait, my rewritten pause-review test passes. The two drag-to-move tests fail on both trees.
  - The drop-caret test failed once with my changes but passed 6/6 on repeat on both trees, so it's flaky.
- **Page picker:** editor-declutter waits for the "Go to page" picker, which only enables once the Typst proof has typeset pages. It never typesets on this machine.
- **Zen mode:** some tests expect a visible formatting toolbar, Bold button or read-aloud control. Those now sit in the collapsed Compositor, because Zen is the default.
- **Changed masthead and drawer:** import and dossier-persistence look for a "File ▾" button and older drawer flows that no longer exist in that form.

**Not run:**
- `manual-instruments`, `manual-living-desk` and `manual-portraits` (the first two have their own config, which needs a production build)
- `instruments-models` (needs model downloads)
- the typing benchmark

The dev servers and the temporary HEAD copy are shut down and removed. The memory note now records how to run these suites and which failures predate this work.

Fixing the 34 is a product call. Pagination is the main one: the e2e tests could be rewritten around the Typst proof, which now appears to do the paging, or the old extension could come back. The other three groups are stale selectors and setup steps I can update directly. Want me to take those on?
